rows.planted: It plans to pay you back over 15 years from what it earns selling the electricity, one of the safest income streams there is.
rows.wrong: Risky word 'safest' (variant of 'safe') describing the income; the next sentence says payments can be late or lower and you could lose money.

rows.planted: Interest paid each year, with all of your money repaid in one amount at the end
rows.wrong: Describes a bullet bond; contradicts the factsheet's equal yearly payments that return a growing part of the EUR 500 each year (pay box and constant EUR 212,706 payment due).

rows.planted: A missed amount stays owed with interest and is paid first from later cash, so you still receive everything you are owed, just later.
rows.wrong: Implied certainty of repayment: drops 'may never be paid in full' and promises missed amounts are always caught up.

rows.planted: It is the only debt, ahead of EUR 3.1M of owner money, so your capital is protected.
rows.wrong: Risky phrase 'capital is protected' (capital-protection claim, not one of the example words); the next sentence says the assets may be worth little.

rows.planted: EUR 110,000, half of one yearly payment, set aside at the start
rows.wrong: Rounded figure now wrong: half of the EUR 212,706 yearly payment is EUR 106,353, not EUR 110,000.

rows.planted: The rest goes to the grid at the market price: about EUR 45 per MWh in 2023, changing every year.
rows.wrong: Wrong year on a dated source: the EUR 45 per MWh market price is the 2025 figure, not 2023.

rows.planted: All power then goes to the grid, and the state steps in through the premium where the hosts left off.
rows.wrong: Implied state backing: suggests the state replaces the hosts as payer, but the premium is only a market top-up and the factsheet says the state does not back the payments.

rows.planted: A bond term (A) stops the owners taking money out in any year when cash available is below 1.01 times the payment due, so from year 9 cash builds up inside the company and covers the gap in years 13-15.
rows.wrong: Changed decimal: the lock-up threshold is 1.10x, not 1.01x (at 1.01x the year-11 cover of 1.04x would not trap cash).

rows.planted: Raising the bond costs EUR 200,000 (8% of the amount: placement fee for the bank and STOKR, legal work, register and token set-up), counted in start-up costs.
rows.wrong: Wrong percentage: EUR 200,000 is 10% of the EUR 2,000,000 raised, not 8%.

rows.planted: Your bond is held for you in an account at a bank or another custodian licensed for financial instruments, so you never handle keys and can pass it to a buyer straight from your banking app (to be confirmed before launch).
rows.wrong: Implied easy exit: presumes a buyer is available and selling is a simple app action, while the factsheet says it is not easy to sell and there may be no buyer.
